A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same paper, including Appendices A–E. Their text, equations, tables and figures can be reliably matched despite layout reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original scene-mapping experiments on 3D-FRONT and ARKitScenes, ablations, robustness analyses and transfer demonstrations in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original quantitative benchmarks, ablations, robustness analyses and qualitative transfer results, including Tables 1–3 and B.1–B.5.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices A and B.8 retain the same contextual descriptor network, contrastive training, affine-plus-local-displacement mapping, outlier rejection and multi-region trajectory procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 3D-FRONT and ARKitScenes coverage, procedural/manual scene pairs, Sim2Real/Real2Sim scenarios, trajectory transfers and object-placement transfers. No dataset or task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across the main benchmarks, Sim2Real and trajectory comparisons. The MAE and DeiT III variants in Table B.1 were already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: Training/evaluation splits, scene-pair counts, point sampling, optimization settings, and PCP, Bijectivity PCP and Chamfer Accuracy metrics and thresholds remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices A–D.

E4.justification: Both retain the embedding and local-displacement ablations, object-cardinality robustness tests, RoI sampling sensitivity analysis, trajectory case studies and affine-initialization failure example. Appendix reflow adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Both report the same point estimates and average runtimes. Neither supplies repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for these experiments.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and B.1–B.5 and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table B.3 retains Sim2Real Chamfer accuracy of 0.55 for 3D Point Feature Field and 0.66 for the proposed method.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives and reasoning are unchanged, including Equations 1–6, A.7–A.8, C.9–C.10 and the isometry criterion in B.8. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions and claims concerning 3D scene analogies, contextual scene maps, robustness, cross-domain applicability and transfer applications.

C2.justification: Performance interpretations and limitations are retained, including incomplete geometry, symmetry ambiguities, affine-initialization failures, training-label requirements and task-dependent correspondence definitions. Appendix D is reflowed without substantive revision.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link to the abstract and explicitly states that it includes code. Existing implementation details and runtime disclosures are unchanged. The PDFs do not establish the linked code's completeness or usability.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Reference-list differences concern citation-page backreferences rather than added literature or revised relationships to prior work.

P1.justification: v2 adds a project/code-access sentence to the abstract and funding acknowledgements before Appendix A, and updates the arXiv version/date. Existing scientific prose and section order are retained.

P2.justification: Figures and table designs are retained, but appendix layout reflows. Table B.3 changes columns, Table B.4 moves from PDF page 10 to 11, and Figure D.12 moves from page 17 to 18.

improvement.justification: The new project/code pointer modestly improves reproducibility information by giving readers an explicit route to implementation resources. Scientific content, evidence and limitations remain unchanged, so the benefit is limited; the supplied PDFs do not verify the linked resources' completeness or usability.
